A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Llamdex despite the changed title and framing. All 15 pages of v2 and 17 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendices B–D report original accuracy, privacy-budget, efficiency, F1, and ablation results.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds evaluated XGBoost experts, Table Diffusion, and DP-OPT comparisons.

M1.justification: V3 introduces an evaluated XGBoost expert option alongside the original MLP expert. The connector architecture, token mapping, encoder/decoder losses, expert insertion, and iterative-feedback procedure remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate natural-language classification questions derived from titanic, wine, bank, nursery, and the appendix adult dataset. The missing-data scenario and Titanic reasoning example already appear in v2. New expert and baseline configurations do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 4 substantially expands the central privacy comparison by adding Table Diffusion and DP-OPT alongside PATE-GAN, SeqPATE, and PromptPATE. The v2 curve labeled Prompt API corresponds to the renamed Expert API comparator in v3. The grouped inference-table footnote also changes to list the expanded DP baseline set.

E3.justification: V3 adds experimental configurations for XGBoost and the two new privacy baselines. DP-OPT introduces validation withholding, boxed-integer answer checking, and chance-probability treatment of missing answer formatting. Existing dataset splits, missing-value masking, and MLP/connector training settings remain unchanged; newly documented retained-baseline settings do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: V3 Table 2 adds an MLP-versus-XGBoost comparison testing dependence on expert architecture. The existing insertion-layer, token-count, token-mapping, padding, expert-weight, alternative-base-LLM, and iterative-reasoning analyses are retained. The appendix plot images are unchanged despite relocation and renumbering.

E5.justification: V2 reports means and standard deviations over five repetitions; v3 specifies means over five independent runs and removes standard deviations from the main accuracy table and Tables 7–11. For example, nursery changes from 51.69±10.88 to 51.69. Figure error bars remain, but uncertainty reporting across the tables is substantially reduced.

E6.justification: V3 adds XGBoost accuracies of 72.81%, 33.75%, 87.94%, and 40.92% on titanic, wine, bank, and nursery, respectively, plus Table Diffusion and DP-OPT curves across privacy budgets. These substantially expand the comparative evidence, including a closely competitive Table Diffusion result on wine. Retained table means and matched plot results are unchanged.

T1.justification: V3 removes the Gaussian-mechanism theorem and the equation equating DP expert training with a noisy minimizer. Section 4 revises the formal data assumption to noncontainment and distinct distributions, and explicitly formulates connector-only optimization with frozen LLM and expert parameters. The DP definition remains; no new proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V3 broadens the framing from DP-protected knowledge transfer to model-based customization services with optional DP and more general expert models. The central model-integration and schema-only-training contributions remain, as do the headline accuracy and inference-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: V3 newly attributes XGBoost's generally lower accuracy to hard thresholds being sensitive to feature-extraction errors, and discusses masking when schemas are private. Its dedicated limitations section largely restates the single-expert and tabular-data boundaries already discussed in v2 Appendix E.

D1.justification: New Appendix E provides extensive baseline hyperparameters, teacher counts, training schedules, LoRA settings, prompts, and parsing instructions. V3 also supplies XGBoost settings, the expert gradient-clipping norm, and dataset/library licensing information. These substantially improve implementation documentation, although v2's DeepSpeed and bf16 disclosures are removed.

R1.justification: The research positioning shifts substantially toward data-based versus API-based customization services and client resource/availability requirements. V3 removes the broader RAG, federated-learning, split-learning, and mixture-of-experts positioning, while adding relevant work on Table Diffusion, DP-OPT, XGBoost, schema masking, and LLM arithmetic/search limitations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, problem definition, and method exposition are extensively rewritten around customization services. Encoder/decoder terminology changes, efficiency and privacy sections exchange order, ablations are reordered, and the appendices gain a contents page and separate hyperparameter, future-direction, and discussion sections.

P2.justification: V3 changes document-wide typesetting, redraws Figure 1, updates architecture labels, and expands Figure 4's curves, legends, and axis ranges. Tables and figures are extensively rearranged; the adult table is transposed, the dataset table gains licenses, and the accuracy table gains an expert row. Existing appendix plots are reused.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens comparative coverage and substantially improves baseline reproducibility through Appendix E. However, removing table-level uncertainty obscures substantial variability already visible in v2, including nursery's 51.69±10.88 and Llama-2 wine's 25.91±14.94. The newly competitive Table Diffusion results also receive little interpretation while broad superiority wording remains. These material benefits and losses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
